evidence: Clear module separation by domain: clienttrader, follower, webtrader, utils, config, exceptions, log, etc., with each module having cohesive responsibilities
Shared core abstractions (IClientTrader, IGridStrategy, IRefreshStrategy, BaseFollower, WebTrader) indicate strong internal cohesion and consistent interface design
No inter-service communication patterns (e.g., no message queues, RPC stubs, or service discovery), and all components run in a single process
Multiple broker-specific trader implementations (e.g., GFClientTrader, HTClientTrader, YHClientTrader) inherit from a common base, showing modular extensibility within one deployment unit
Server module uses Flask to expose a local API, but remains tightly integrated with core trading modules rather than being decoupled as a separate service
Repository depth of 3 and 5 packages suggest a flat but organized hierarchy typical of modular monoliths
Low average fan-out (1.64) indicates modules depend on few others, supporting modularity without distributed complexity
risks: Tight coupling between UI automation (pywinauto) and business logic may hinder testability and maintainability
Multiple inheritance hierarchies (e.g., ClientTrader → BaseLoginClientTrader → concrete traders) increase complexity and risk of fragile base class problem
Shared state in follower threads and trader instances may cause concurrency issues in multi-strategy scenarios
